chats.answer:
If you're looking for a dash cam with parking mode, I'd recommend one that records both while driving and while your car is parked, especially if you're concerned about hit-and-runs, door dings, or vandalism.

The most important feature is buffered parking recording—it saves footage from before an impact or motion event, not just afterward.

What to look for

Front + rear cameras: Capture incidents from both directions.

Buffered parking mode: Records several seconds before an event.

Low-voltage protection: Prevents the dash cam from draining your car battery.

Good night vision: Important for parking garages and dark streets.

Hardwire kit or dedicated battery: Most dash cams need one of these to record after the engine is off.

chats.answer:
If you're looking for a dash cam with parking mode, I recommend choosing one that records while your car is parked and the engine is off.

There are three important parking features:

Buffered parking recording: Saves footage from a few seconds before an impact or motion event, so you can see what caused it.

Impact detection: Automatically records when someone hits your parked car.

24/7 time-lapse recording: Continuously monitors your car using low-frame-rate recording to conserve storage and power.

For most people, I'd recommend a front-and-rear dash cam with buffered parking mode, a hardwire kit, and low-voltage battery protection.
